props.gloss_en: R' Levi: like the date palm -- as this palm has but one heart, so Israel have but one heart toward their Father in heaven
the blessing over the lulav is said seven days
the blessing over the sukkah is said one day
lulav, whose nights break off from its days -- each day is a mitzva by itself
sukkah, whose nights do not break off from its days -- all seven are like one long day
the blessing over the sukkah is said seven days
the blessing over the lulav is said one day
sukkah is Torah law [all seven] -- seven
lulav is rabbinic -- one day suffices for it
Rav Yosef: take Rabba bar bar Chana's [version of R' Yochanan] in your hand
for all the amoraim stand with him on sukkah
one who makes a lulav for himself says: Blessed... who has kept us alive, sustained us and brought us to this time
taking it to fulfil [the mitzva] he says: ... who sanctified us with His mitzvot and commanded us concerning the taking of the lulav
one who makes a sukkah for himself says: Blessed... who has kept us alive...
entering to sit in it he says: ... who sanctified us with His mitzvot and commanded us to sit in the sukkah
here [the baraita's lulav all seven]: while the Temple stands
there [R' Yochanan's lulav one day]: when the Temple does not stand
[the sukkah contradiction] is a tannaitic dispute
tefillin: every time one dons them he blesses over them -- the words of Rabbi
and the Sages say: he blesses only in the morning
Abaye: the halakha follows Rabbi [on the tefillin blessing]
Rava: the halakha follows the Sages
Rav Mari: I saw Rava not act by his own ruling -- he would rise early, go to the privy, wash, don tefillin and bless; and when he needed to go again, again wash, don and bless
and we too act as Rabbi, and bless all seven [days]
Mar Zutra: I saw Rav Pappi bless whenever he donned tefillin
the Sages of Rav Ashi's house blessed whenever they touched them
[it is] the mitzva of lulav all seven [days]
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: the first day -- the mitzva of lulav
from then on -- a mitzva of the Elders
R' Yitzchak [as first cited]: every day is a mitzva of the Elders
but we hold that the first day is Torah law
Rav: one who lights a Chanukah light must bless
R' Yirmeya: one who sees a Chanukah light must bless
Rav Yehuda: on the first day the one who lights blesses three
the one who sees blesses two
from then on, the one who lights blesses two
and the one who sees blesses one
and what does he bless? Blessed... who sanctified us with His mitzvot and commanded us to light the Chanukah light
and where did He command us? from 'you shall not turn aside' (Devarim 17:11)
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: from 'ask your father and he will tell you' (Devarim 32:7)
what does he omit [after the first day]? the blessing of the time
if it was already made and standing: if he can renew something in it, he blesses [shehecheyanu]
if not, when he enters to sit in it he blesses two
Rav Ashi: I saw Rav Kahana say all of them over the kiddush cup
the baraita: if many mitzvot were before him, he says: ... who commanded us concerning the mitzvot
R' Yehuda: he blesses over each one by itself
R' Zeira: the halakha follows R' Yehuda
R' Zeira: R' Yehuda's reason is the verse 'Blessed is the Lord day by day' (Tehillim 68:20)
does one bless Him by day and not by night? rather it comes to tell you: each and every day give Him blessings fitting to it
here too -- for each and every thing give Him blessings fitting to it
come and see: the way of flesh and blood is not like the way of the Holy One
the way of flesh and blood: an empty vessel holds, a full one does not
but the way of the Holy One: a full one holds, an empty one does not
as it is said: 'and it shall be, if you will surely listen' (Devarim 28:1) -- if you listen, you will listen; and if not, you will not listen
another reading: if you listen to the old, you will listen to the new; and if your heart turns away, you will no longer listen
